title: Introducing Luel Labs
summary: An end-to-end multimodal data lab, from our globally deployed contributor network and multimodal QA engine through to research and development.
body_markdown:
Today we're launching[Luel Labs](https://www.luel.ai/lab) : our end-to-end multimodal data lab, built on top of our globally deployed contributor network and multimodal QA engine.


## The engine underneath


More than 900,000 contributors across 96+ countries complete audio, video and image tasks and are paid per accepted submission. Every submission is consented, and speech runs through quality assurance before anything downstream can use it.


That engine is what makes the Labs possible. Collection and quality assurance built for the platform can be pointed at anything: a native-speaker speech corpus for a language with almost no recorded data, real overlapping conversation instead of studio reads, the checks themselves. Results are then measured on public benchmarks, so they stay comparable to everyone else's.


## From the tips of the Himalayas to across the Sahara


Speech comes first. The platform records every modality, but speech is where the distance between what people speak and what technology serves is widest. Most of the world's languages have almost no recorded, transcribed audio at all, and a contributor network that pays native speakers to create it changes what can be built.

UNESCO's Atlas documents 8,324 languages; open research covers 1,107 with a single-speaker voice each; the most multilingual commercial system speaks 74. The sliver is where the industry is; the rest is where our contributors are.


We're delivering **TTS for Tibetan and Dzongkha** , shippable, licensed voices for two languages the major platforms did not list when we checked, and dialect voices for **Masri and Darija** . All four ship as[Luel Speech](https://www.luel.ai/blog/luel-speech-is-now-available) , public today.


Masri is the Arabic that more than a hundred million people actually speak, not the formal MSA that generic systems fall back to. It code-switches into English and French and reads numbers and dates in dialect-specific ways, and general multilingual voices tend to mispronounce it or slip into a foreign accent. On a 50-sentence Egyptian Arabic benchmark scored by a panel of eight independent ASR judges, our shipped voice reached a character error rate of 0.1633 median and 0.1604 mean, the lowest of the seven systems tested, ahead of VoiceTut, ElevenLabs v2 and v3, Azure Neural ar-EG, NileTTS and an untuned SILMA base. The gap to the nearest system is 0.0073, inside this design's resolution of about ±0.011, so it is an ordering rather than a separation. Competitor audio was synthesised on 2026-07-06 and was not re-synthesised against our final arms. The full record is on the[Egyptian Arabic benchmark](https://www.luel.ai/lab/benchmarks/egyptian-arabic-tts) .


Each voice is built from scratch on its own native-speaker corpus, never a multilingual checkpoint borrowed from the language next door. The[Moroccan Darija](https://www.luel.ai/lab/benchmarks/moroccan-darija-tts) board shows its own result, with the axes where we trail.


## Foundational research on messy, real-world data


The rest of the program applies **speaker separation** , **conversational-overlap evaluation** , **STT modeling** , **data integrity** and **speech understanding** to audio the industry usually throws away.


Separation is the clearest example. Hand[Luel Multi-Speaker Separation](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/multi-speaker-separation) a recording of a conversation and it returns a separate recording for each speaker. The harder test is what it does when only one person is talking: the right answer is one speaker, not an invented second voice. Radio, classrooms and oral histories all arrive as overlapping speech, and separation is how they become usable data.


A data-integrity program runs under all of it, pointed at the platform's own checks and measurements.


## Where this goes next


The work above shares one direction: pick a place where the data is missing, use the platform to create it, and put the result on a public benchmark. The same build-from-scratch principle spans specialist voices, separation for radio, classrooms and oral histories, and quality assurance across audio, video and images.


New voices, corpora, and benchmarked results continue on[Luel Labs](https://www.luel.ai/lab) .
